Frequently Asked Questions

If your question isn’t here, just text us — or email hello@mayaanddevon.party. We’d rather you ask twice than not at all.

Is the ceremony outdoors?

Yes — we’re getting married in the lower meadow at Stonewall Hill Farm, weather permitting. If the weather doesn’t cooperate, we have a tented backup plan inside the barn courtyard. Either way, plan for grass and bring a layer for after sunset. The ceremony itself is short (about 30 minutes) and the chairs are comfortable.

Can I bring a plus-one?

The names on your invitation envelope are the people we’ve invited. If your invitation says “Sam Wu & guest,” you have a plus-one — please give us their full name on your RSVP. If your invitation lists only your name and you’d like to bring someone, just text us. We’re not precious about it; we’d rather know in advance than have a missing place card situation.

Are kids welcome?

With great affection: we’re having an adults-only wedding, with two exceptions — nursing babies and the small handful of kids in the wedding party. The reason is selfish: we want all of you to dance, drink, and stay until midnight. If you need help arranging a sitter, the front desks at both the Lazy Crow Inn and the Catskill Lodge keep a list of trusted local sitters, and we’re happy to make introductions.

What does “garden formal” mean?

Think: the most beautiful version of an outdoor wedding on a working farm. Long sundresses, linen suits in dusty colors, midi skirts, jumpsuits, suits without ties. Flowers and dusty pastels are encouraged; black is fine; white, ivory, or cream is for the bride. The main rule is shoes you can walk on grass in — no stilettos, please. Block heels, wedges, flats, or dressy sneakers will all be much happier. See the details page for examples.

Will there be vegetarian, vegan, or gluten-free options?

Yes to all of it — the caterer is wonderful at this. Please flag your dietary needs on your RSVP so we can give the kitchen accurate numbers, and they’ll prepare a beautiful plate for every restriction. If you have a severe allergy (anaphylactic, celiac, etc.), please note that specifically in the “allergies” field — we’ll follow up directly to make sure you’re safe.

What’s the weather usually like in mid-September?

Generally lovely. Average daytime highs in Roxbury for September 19 sit around 70°F (21°C), with overnight lows around 50°F (10°C). It’s typically the start of the leaves turning — yellows and oranges, not yet peak — and the air at night is cool and dry. That said, the Catskills can do whatever they want, so plan layers. A light jacket or wrap for the evening will make a real difference.

I don’t have a car — how do I get there?

You have a few options. The easiest are: (1) the Trailways bus from Port Authority to Margaretville, then a 15-minute Uber to your hotel; or (2) carpooling from NYC with other guests (we’ll share a spreadsheet in August). If you’re staying at the Lazy Crow Inn or the Catskill Lodge, we’ll run shuttles to and from the venue, so you only need to get yourself as far as the hotel. Full transit details are on the travel page.

Is there parking at the venue?

Yes — the farm has a large upper field for guest parking, and golf carts will run all afternoon to shuttle anyone who would rather ride than walk the short hill down to the ceremony site. Parking is free. You can leave a car overnight if you need to call a ride; we’ll have a list of guests who plan to do that so the venue knows.

Where should I stay?

We’ve held small room blocks at the Lazy Crow Inn ($$$, the nicer option) and the Catskill Lodge ($$, a great mid-range pick). Both will run shuttles to the venue. There’s also a deep supply of AirBnB cabins in the area if you’re a group of four or more and want to make a weekend of it. All three options, with detail, are on the travel page.

Is there a welcome event Friday night?

Yes — we’re hosting a casual welcome dinner at Peekamoose Restaurant on Friday, September 18, from 6:30 to 9:00 PM, for any guest who’s in town. It’s an open invitation, but please let us know on your RSVP if you’re planning to come so we can give the restaurant a count. Dress code: whatever you wore on the drive up.

Is there anything happening Sunday morning?

Yes! We’re doing a relaxed brunch at the Catskill Lodge on Sunday, September 20, from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM. Stop by whenever, eat whatever you can fit, say goodbye. No RSVP needed for this one — just show up if you’re still in town.

Can I take photos during the ceremony?

We’re asking for an “unplugged” ceremony — phones away, no photos, just be there with us. We have a wonderful photographer (Imani Foster) who will capture everything. Once the ceremony is over, please take a thousand photos and tag us. We’ll share Imani’s gallery link in early October so you can grab anything you’d like.

What time should I arrive?

Aim to be at the venue between 1:15 and 1:45 PM. The ceremony starts at 2:00 PM sharp, and we’d rather have you parked and seated with a few minutes to breathe than scrambling. If you’re taking a hotel shuttle, the vans leave the lobbies at 12:50 PM (Lazy Crow) and 1:05 PM (Catskill Lodge). Try to be a few minutes early — they don’t wait.

What if I have an accessibility need?

Please tell us. The venue is accessible — the barn has a ramp entrance and an accessible single-stall restroom, and golf carts will be running constantly to anyone who would rather not walk the grass hill down to the ceremony. If you need specific accommodations (mobility, hearing, sensory, dietary, anything), there’s a dedicated field on the RSVP form. We’d much rather over-prepare than miss something. No detail is too small.

What’s the cell service like?

Honestly? Spotty. Verizon and T-Mobile both work okay around the village of Roxbury and at the hotels. The farm itself has reliable Wi-Fi (we’ll share the password) but cell coverage drops off once you’re inside the barn. Plan to be a little unreachable — it’s actually nice.

Can I post photos on social media?

Yes, after the ceremony. We’d love it — please tag us if you do. We’re using #MayaAndDevon2026 as a loose collecting hashtag, mostly so we can find everything later. The only thing we ask is no posts during the ceremony itself (see the unplugged-ceremony note above).

Will there be a gift table at the wedding?

No — please don’t bring physical gifts to the venue. We have a long drive home Sunday and a small car. If you’d like to send something, all four registries (and a few non-registry alternatives) are on the registry page, and everything ships directly. Your presence really is enough; we mean that.
